stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab disrupts telecom services, restoration work begins
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab disrupts telecom services, restoration work begins
stories.summary: New Delhi, Oct 31 : The government is is undertaking restoration efforts and monitoring the telecom network situation to ensure the continuity of essential communication services in the affected areas, after Cyclone Arnab hit along the coast of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha. Widespread heavy rainfall, flash floods, tree falls and power infrastructure disruptions affected telecom services across parts of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and adjoining regions. The Department of Telecommunications (DoT), in coordination with Telecom Service Providers (TSPs), is undertaking restoration efforts. “Significant progress has been achieved in restoring network connectivity across Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, with particular focus on resolving power supply disruptions and restoring optical fibre connectivity,” according to the Ministry of Communications. “Emergency connectivity arrangements, including ICR and COW deployments, are being maintained to facilitate uninterrupted communication for citizens and support relief and restoration activities in the affected regions,” it said in a statement. In Andhra Pradesh, overall telecom network availability has reached 99.18 per cent. In Odisha, the telecom network situation in Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal districts has been gradually improving with the easing of rainfall and receding of floodwaters. Telecom Service Providers (TSPs) have initiated restoration work at affected sites, resulting in progressive improvement in network connectivity and a reduction in service disruptions. All TSPs are making sustained efforts on a priority basis to restore the remaining affected sites and ensure early normalisation of telecom services and uninterrupted connectivity for the public, informed the ministry. Intra Circle Roaming (ICR) is a telecom arrangement where a mobile subscriber connects to another operator’s (TSP’s) network within the same telecom circle (region). This allows users to access mobile services even if their own operator (TSP) has no coverage in that specific area. It plays a critical role during natural disasters when mobile infrastructure is damaged. During the time of disaster, if mobile infrastructure is damaged in a region, DoT issues instructions to Telecom Service Providers to implement ICR. --IANS

stories.headline: Sikkim Shivers as Cyclone Arnab Remnants Trigger 11.4°C Temperature Drop and Red Alert in Gangtok
stories.title: Sikkim Shivers as Cyclone Arnab Remnants Trigger 11.4°C Temperature Drop and Red Alert in Gangtok
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Sikkim: The severe weather trailing the aftermath of Cyclone Arnab has sent shockwaves through the Himalayan state of Sikkim.
The capital city of Gangtok experienced a dramatic 11.4°C plunge in its maximum temperature, transforming the typical post-monsoon chill into a freezing, winter-like environment within hours.
The system, which originally tore through the Andhra Pradesh coast as a very severe cyclonic storm, has since weakened into a low-pressure area over land.
However, its moisture-heavy tailwinds continue to batter the high-altitude terrains of Northeast India.
Official records indicate that Gangtok's daytime temperature plummeted to just 14°C, hovering unusually close to its minimum temperature of 12.4°C.
The sudden chill has been compounded by severe precipitation across the state.
Within a 24-hour testing window, Gangtok recorded 21.2 mm of rainfall, while the historic town of Yuksom endured a staggering 60.8 mm downpour.

Meanwhile, higher reaches—including popular tourist spots like Nathu La, Kupup, Tsomgo Lake, and the Gnathang Valley—were hit by unseasonal heavy snowfall, prompting swift snow-clearing operations by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO).
Addressing the developing system, Debapriya Roy, Head of the India Meteorological Department (IMD) Gangtok, confirmed the severe atmospheric transition.
"The cyclone Arnab weakened and has converted into a low-pressure area," Roy stated.
"Due to the effect of the remnants of cyclone Arnab in Sikkim, there is a possibility of rainfall today and tomorrow.
Today, heavy rainfall is also likely at one or two places."

stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab wreaks havoc in Odisha: 3 dead, thousands affected by floods
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab wreaks havoc in Odisha: 3 dead, thousands affected by floods
stories.summary: Cyclone Arnab wreaks havoc in Odisha: 3 dead, thousands affected by floods
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: At least three people, including a nine-month-old baby, died in a landslide in Odisha as heavy rainfall triggered by cyclone ‘Arnab’ battered the state’s southern districts on Friday, flooding hundreds of villages and leaving thousands of people affected.

The cyclone, initially forecast to have a greater impact on neighbouring Andhra Pradesh and cause relatively less damage in Odisha, changed course and caused extensive destruction in Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal districts, chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi said.
“The state was expecting damages in Malkangiri district bordering Andhra Pradesh, but ‘Arnab’ wreaked havoc in Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal districts,” Majhi said.
Continuous heavy rainfall led to a sharp rise in river levels and triggered nearly a dozen landslides across the affected districts.
In one such incident in Kandhamal, a couple and their nine-month-old son were buried in a landslide and died, a minister said.
The chief minister announced an ex gratia of Rs 4 lakh each for the families of the deceased.

With large parts of southern Odisha submerged, the state government has stepped up rescue and relief operations, deploying four helicopters belonging to the Indian Navy and the Indian Coast Guard to airdrop food packets in flood-hit areas of Ganjam district.

Following an aerial survey of the affected areas along with disaster management minister Suresh Pujari, Majhi said the government had immediately sought assistance from the Centre after receiving information about the cyclone's change in course.
Special relief commissioner Rajesh P Patil said food packets had been airdropped at 21 identified locations in Ganjam.

Teams from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) were also using boats to deliver cooked food to people stranded in inundated villages, despite difficult weather conditions and strong water currents.
More than 23,000 people were staying in relief camps, although the number of those stranded in flood-hit areas was considerably higher, Pujari said.
Of the 313 rescue teams deployed across Odisha, more than 100 were operating in Ganjam and Gajapati districts.

stories.headline: Cyclone Arnab aftermath: Tens of thousands stranded in Odisha villages as fresh weather system threatens more rain
stories.title: Cyclone Arnab aftermath: Tens of thousands stranded in Odisha villages as fresh weather system threatens more rain
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Odisha government has stepped up rescue and relief operations across southern districts battered by exceptionally heavy rain brought by Cyclone Arnab on October 28.
The rainfall may also have been influenced a second cyclonic system to the storm's northeast.

The downpour sent rivers, including the Rushikulya and Mahendratanaya, swelling, triggering floods and landslides that washed away roads and bridges and left villages marooned across seven districts—Ganjam, Gajapati, Kandhamal, Koraput, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur and Rayagada.
Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal are among the worst-affected districts.
Several villages remain cut off by floodwaters, with food and other essential supplies being delivered by helicopter.
According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Patrapur in Ganjam recorded the highest rainfall, at 546 mm, followed by Sorada, also in Ganjam, with 503 mm.
G Udayagiri in Kandhamal received 462 mm, Mahendragarh in Gajapati 458 mm, while Sanakhemundi and Chikiti in Ganjam received 388 mm and 309 mm, respectively.

Speaking to journalists on October 30, Suresh Pujari, the state's revenue and disaster-management minister, said water levels in several rivers had risen sharply, with some exceeding their danger marks and posing a serious flood threat.
According to state officials, 299 villages across 22 blocks in Ganjam district and 711 villages across seven blocks in Gajapati had been affected.
Around 42,500 people in Ganjam and 20,000 in Gajapati were affected.

National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) and Fire Services personnel had evacuated 11,882 people in Ganjam and 17,441 in Gajapati, moving them to flood and cyclone shelters.
Strong currents have prevented rescue teams from reaching some of the worst-affected areas.

stories.headline: NEADS Launches Flood Preparedness Initiative in Upper Assam
stories.title: NEADS Launches Flood Preparedness Initiative in Upper Assam
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: JORHAT: North-East Affected Area Development Society (NEADS), a grassroots development organisation based in Assam, has launched a learning initiative to strengthen community-led flood preparedness, early warning, and timely humanitarian action across Upper Assam.

Supported through the Start Fund under its flooding response initiative, the programme will draw on the experiences of the 2026 floods, particularly in Upper Assam, while connecting community-level learning with wider experiences from flood-affected areas across the Eastern Himalayan region.

A central focus of the initiative is to understand the gap between early warning and early action, particularly why the availability of flood and weather-related information does not always translate into timely preparedness measures and humanitarian assistance.

stories.headline: IPS officer who led Pahalgam attack probe bags Home Minister’s medal
stories.title: IPS officer who led Pahalgam attack probe bags Home Minister’s medal
stories.summary: Srinagar, Oct 31: IPS officer Sandeep Chaudhary, a 2012-batch officer who headed the investigation into the Pahalgam terror attack, has been awarded the ‘Kendriya Grihmantri Dakshata Padak’ for outstanding work in investigation. The medal is among the awards conferred on 490 personnel from various States, Union Territories, Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and Central Police Organisations (CPOs) for the year 2026, according to the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). The Ministry said the medal recognises excellent work, promotes high professional standards and boosts the morale of police and other personnel. “The award was instituted by the Ministry of Home Affairs through a notification dated February 1, 2024, and is conferred on personnel of police forces, security organisations, intelligence wings, CAPFs, CPOs, the National Security Guard, Assam Rifles and forensic science departments for excellence in operations, outstanding investigation, exceptional performance, intelligence services and meritorious work in forensic science,” the Ministry said. The medal is announced every year on October 31 to mark the birth anniversary of Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.—(KNO)

stories.headline: I will serve the people of India till my last breath: PM Modi
stories.title: I will serve the people of India till my last breath: PM Modi
stories.summary: Bhildi (Gujarat), Oct 30: Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Friday that he would serve the people of India till his last breath, an assertion coming days after Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge’s remark, “Modi ka baap bhi jayega”. He was addressing a gathering after inaugurating the Bharat Bovine Breeding and Research Centre at Bhildi in Gujarat’s Banaskantha district, launching and laying the foundation stone for development projects worth Rs 14,000 crore. “Jeevan ke antim kshan tak janta ki seva main hi juta rahunga (I will continue to serve the people until my last breath),” Modi said. In an apparent jab at the Opposition, he said there are some people who get happiness when the country faces difficulty. “They spread rumours after the Iran war that farmers would not get fertilisers, and people would not get LPG, as they wanted to defame Modi,” the PM said. Modi said his government has always prioritised the welfare of farmers and empowered them. “Amid global uncertainties, fertiliser prices saw a huge jump, but our govt did not let the burden fall on farmers,” he said, adding that the government has given Rs 4.5 lakh crore to small farmers under PM-Kisan Samman Nidhi.

stories.headline: India slams global energy disruptions through sanctions, chokepoints
stories.title: India slams global energy disruptions through sanctions, chokepoints
stories.summary: The Minister emphasised that continuous distortions of energy markets through obstacles, sanctions and chokepoints were happening with increasing frequency, greater complexity and wider impact
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar strongly disapproved of disruptions in global oil supplies through sanctions and chokepoints, saying deliberate attacks on energy trade and infrastructure were a calculated strategy to hold prices hostage.

Mr. Jaishankar’s remarks at the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta on Friday (October 30, 2026) came amid American sanctions on the sale of Iranian oil and disruption to energy supplies from West Asia and the decision to lift sanctions on the sale of Russian diesel.
The Minister said that the world was staring at an energy crisis not of production, but of unpredictability and disruption, unaffordable costs, and challenges of access.
Mr. Jaishankar, in a post on X, said he highlighted that deliberate attacks on energy trade and infrastructure were a calculated strategy to hold energy prices hostage.
“The G20 must display both understanding and leadership to keep energy markets open and predictable,” he said at the meeting convened by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
The Minister emphasised that continuous distortions of energy markets through obstacles, sanctions and chokepoints were happening with increasing frequency, greater complexity and wider impact.
Mr. Jaishankar said he underscored that there appears to be little regard for the predicament of low-income countries.
The Minister said that convenient distinctions are being drawn between oil and gas.
“Selective carve-outs speak for themselves,” he said.
Mr. Jaishankar said he reiterated that the knock-on effects and mutual dependence in a globalised market should not be underestimated.
He reaffirmed that India needs reliable and predictable LPG supplies for its clean cooking needs.
Mr. Jaishankar reiterated that India’s National Mission on critical minerals spans exploration to recycling.

Mr. Jaishankar’s remarks at the G20 Foreign Ministers’ Meeting in Atlanta on Friday (October 30, 2026) came amid American sanctions on the sale of Iranian oil and disruption to energy supplies from West Asia and the decision to lift sanctions on the sale of Russian diesel.

Mr. Jaishankar, in a post on X, said he highlighted that deliberate attacks on energy trade and infrastructure were a calculated strategy to hold energy prices hostage.
“The G20 must display both understanding and leadership to keep energy markets open and predictable,” he said at the meeting convened by U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
The Minister emphasised that continuous distortions of energy markets through obstacles, sanctions and chokepoints were happening with increasing frequency, greater complexity and wider impact.
Mr. Jaishankar said he underscored that there appears to be little regard for the predicament of low-income countries.
The Minister said that convenient distinctions are being drawn between oil and gas.
“Selective carve-outs speak for themselves,” he said.
Mr. Jaishankar said he reiterated that the knock-on effects and mutual dependence in a globalised market should not be underestimated.

stories.summary: Victor Lalawmpuia, Nibas Meetei Wahengbam and R. Lalremruatfela scored twice each for the Blue Colts, while Cuba’s reply was too little too late in India’s 6-4 win.

article_sentences: India ended its campaign at the FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival 2026 on a winning note, defeating Cuba 6-4 in the 87th-place play-off at the Hovsan Competition Complex Pitch 1B in Baku on Friday, October 30, 2026.
Victor Lalawmpuia, Nibas Meetei Wahengbam and R. Lalremruatfela scored twice each as the Blue Colts won their 10th and final fixture of the tournament.
India built a commanding 6-1 advantage before Cuba struck three late goals to narrow the margin.
Bibiano Fernandes’ side was on the charge from the outset and needed less than a minute to take the lead.
Lalawmpuia stole possession from Cuba’s central defender, evaded a challenge and calmly placed his shot into the bottom-right corner.
India doubled their advantage in the sixth minute through a well-worked move down the left.
Lalremruatfela and Muhammad Sohil Khan combined before the latter delivered a cross across the face of goal, beyond the reach of the Cuban defence and goalkeeper.
An unmarked Nibas arrived at the far post to tap home.
Cuba responded by testing Dhannya Desai from distance and close range, but the India goalkeeper produced several important saves to preserve his side’s two-goal cushion.
India extended its lead in the 12th minute following a set piece.
Sohil floated a free-kick into the area from the left, and although Cuba cleared the initial delivery, Nara Meitei Loushambam sent the ball back into the penalty box.
Lalremruatfela was left unmarked and tapped it home to make it 3-0.
